claim: The evolution of multicellularity occurred in at least 25 separate lineages.
source: The evolution of multicellularity was transformative for life on Earth, occurring in at least 25 separate lineages (Grosberg and Strathmann, 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Grosberg and Strathmann, 2007

claim: Self-assembly is fundamentally subject to random noise.
source: Self-assembly, however, is fundamentally subject to random noise (Zeravcic and Brenner, 2014; Szavits-Nossan et al., 2014; Damavandi and Lubensky, 2019) that affects the final emergent structure (Michel and Yunker, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies on self-assembly and noise

claim: The physiology of multicellular organisms can depend sensitively on the geometry of cellular packing.
source: The physiology of multicellular organisms can depend sensitively on the geometry of cellular packing (Bi et al., 2015b; Drescher et al., 2016; Jacobeen et al., 2018b; Brunet et al., 2019; Schmideder et al., 2021)
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claim: Extant multicellular organisms can either suppress or leverage variability in the process of reliably generating structures.
source: Recent work has shown that extant multicellular organisms can either suppress (Hong et al., 2016) or leverage (Haas et al., 2018) variability in the process of reliably generating structures
evidence: Supported by citations to Hong et al., 2016 and Haas et al., 2018

claim: The free space associated with individual cells in snowflake yeast closely fits a modified gamma distribution.
source: We find that despite large differences in cellular organization, the free space associated with individual cells in both organisms closely fits a modified gamma distribution, consistent with maximum entropy predictions originally developed for granular materials.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract

claim: The free space associated with individual cells in Volvox carteri closely fits a modified gamma distribution.
source: We find that despite large differences in cellular organization, the free space associated with individual cells in both organisms closely fits a modified gamma distribution, consistent with maximum entropy predictions originally developed for granular materials.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract

claim: Snowflake yeast grow via incomplete cytokinesis, generating branched structures in which mother-daughter cells remain attached by permanently bonded cell walls.
source: Snowflake yeast grow via incomplete cytokinesis, generating branched structures in which mother-daughter cells remain attached by permanently bonded cell walls (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by description and reference to Figure 1A

claim: New buds appear on ellipsoidal snowflake yeast cells at a polar angle ⟨θ⟩=42°±23°.
source: New buds appear on ellipsoidal cells at a polar angle ⟨θ⟩=42%±23% and azimuthal angle ϕ that is randomly distributed (⟨ϕ⟩=180%±104%, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: The azimuthal angle of new buds on snowflake yeast cells is randomly distributed with ⟨ϕ⟩=180°±104°.
source: New buds appear on ellipsoidal cells at a polar angle ⟨θ⟩=42%±23% and azimuthal angle ϕ that is randomly distributed (⟨ϕ⟩=180%±104%, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: The distribution of Voronoi volumes in snowflake yeast closely matched the predicted k-gamma distribution with k=2.88.
source: The distribution of cellular Voronoi volumes closely matched the predicted k-gamma distribution (Figure 1C, k=2.88).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C

claim: Volvox carteri embryos arise as a spherical cellular monolayer from palintomic cell divisions with incomplete cytokinesis.
source: V. carteri embryos arise as a spherical cellular monolayer from palintomic cell divisions with incomplete cytokinesis, which leaves the cells attached via cytoplasmic bridges.
evidence: Description of Volvox development based on established knowledge

claim: Volvox carteri has approximately 1000 somatic cells embedded on the surface of a translucent sphere of extracellular matrix.
source: The approximately 1000 somatic cells remain embedded on the surface of a translucent sphere of extracellular matrix (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by description and Figure 1B

claim: Volvox Voronoi solid angles are positively correlated at distances as large as Q=10.
source: We find that Volvox Voronoi solid angles are positively correlated at distances as large as Q=10 (Figure 3A).
evidence: Supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 3A

claim: Flocculating yeast groups exhibit a much larger coefficient of variation in size compared to snowflake yeast groups.
source: We find that flocculating yeast groups exhibit a much larger coefficient of variation in size compared to snowflake yeast groups (Pentz et al., 2020; Figure 5D).
evidence: Supported by data from Pentz et al., 2020 shown in Figure 5D

claim: Within the squirmer model, motility is essentially insensitive to area inhomogeneities.
source: Thus, within the squirmer model, motility is essentially insensitive to area inhomogeneities.
evidence: Derived from theoretical analysis of the squirmer model

claim: The maximum entropy distribution is expected if cell neighborhood volumes are determined independently of each other.
source: This distribution is expected if cell neighborhood volumes are determined independently of each other (while still conforming to the total volume constraint).
evidence: Theoretical explanation of when maximum entropy predictions apply

claim: Correlations between the size of separate volumes will lead to deviations from maximum entropy predictions.
source: In other words, volumes must be set randomly; correlations between the size of separate volumes will lead to deviations from maximum entropy predictions.
evidence: Theoretical explanation of when deviations from maximum entropy occur

claim: Maximum entropy statistics hold in granular materials despite strict force and torque balance conditions.
source: For example, maximum entropy statistics hold in granular materials, despite the fact that they must obey strict force and torque balance conditions (Aste and Di Matteo, 2008; Snoeijer et al., 2004; Bi et al., 2015a).
evidence: Supported by citations to studies on granular materials

claim: The mean cellular aspect ratio of petite yeast was α≡a/b=1.28±0.20.
source: We measured the mean cellular aspect ratio to be α≡a/b=1.28±0.20.
evidence: Measured from SEM images

claim: The local hexatic order in Volvox somatic cell arrangement is low.
source: From a physics perspective, the local hexatic order in the somatic cell arrangement is low (see Materials and methods).
evidence: Stated in the text with reference to Materials and methods

claim: Ψ6 for Volvox carteri somatic cells is 0.03±0.01.
source: We calculated Ψ6 separately for each of six different organisms; we report Ψ6=0.03±0.01.
evidence: Calculated from experimental data

claim: The size to which snowflake yeast grow depends strongly on the aspect ratio of its constituent cells.
source: The size to which snowflake yeast grow depends strongly on the aspect ratio of its constituent cells; more elongated cells allow the growth of larger clusters before strain from cellular packing causes group fragmentation (Jacobeen et al., 2018a; Jacobeen et al., 2018b).
evidence: Supported by citations to Jacobeen et al., 2018a and 2018b

claim: Group size in engineered yeast was more heritable than the underlying cellular trait of aspect ratio.
source: Recently, experiments with engineered yeast showed that this emergent multicellular trait, group size, was in fact more heritable than the underlying cellular trait upon which it was based (cellular aspect ratio), despite the fact that the mutations engineered in this system only affected cellular aspect ratio directly (Zamani-Dahaj et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zamani-Dahaj et al., 2021

claim: Gamma-distributed cell neighborhood sizes are a general feature of multicellularity, arising from conserved statistics of cellular packing.
source: Together with simulations of diverse growth morphologies, these results suggest that gamma-distributed cell neighborhood sizes are a general feature of multicellularity, arising from conserved statistics of cellular packing.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental and simulation results

claim: Entropic cellular packing ensures a degree of predictability despite noise, facilitating parent-offspring fidelity even in the absence of developmental regulation.
source: This 'entropic' cellular packing ensures a degree of predictability despite noise, facilitating parent-offspring fidelity even in the absence of developmental regulation.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a key finding

claim: Volvox carteri first evolved multicellularity in the Triassic.
source: Second, we used the green microalga Volvox carteri, a member of the volvocine algae that first evolved multicellularity in the Triassic (Starr, 1969; Herron et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Starr, 1969 and Herron et al., 2009

claim: Six-fold coordination is the most frequent local arrangement of somatic cells in Volvox.
source: While six-fold coordination is the most frequent local arrangement of somatic cells, the fact that the cells are embedded in a surface with spherical topology requires there to be 'defects' with differing coordination number (e.g. 5,7), and these are found interspersed around the spheroid.
evidence: Observation from experimental data

claim: Deviations from maximum entropy predictions encode important information about additional correlations that can arise via developmental regulation or interactions with the environment.
source: Deviations from maximum entropy predictions therefore encode important information about additional correlations that can arise via a variety of sources, such as developmental regulation or interactions with the environment.
evidence: Interpretation of the significance of deviations from predictions

claim: Random noise can lead to highly reproducible multicellular traits such as the cell packing distribution.
source: In this context, our results demonstrate that random noise can itself lead to highly reproducible multicellular traits such as the cell packing distribution.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the study's findings

claim: Entropic packing is not necessarily adaptive; it can readily emerge as a consequence of random cellular reproduction or interactions.
source: It is thus important to note that entropic packing is not necessarily adaptive; it can readily emerge as a consequence of random cellular reproduction or interactions.
evidence: Interpretation of the evolutionary implications of entropic packing

claim: Parent-offspring heredity arising from entropic packing could play a crucial role in the evolutionary transition to multicellularity.
source: Such parent-offspring heredity could play a crucial role in the evolutionary transition to multicellularity, providing a mechanism for nascent multicellular organisms to participate in the evolutionary process without first having to possess genetically regulated development.
evidence: Speculation about evolutionary implications

claim: Fragmentation is a common mode of multicellular reproduction.
source: Finally, as fragmentation is a common mode of multicellular reproduction (Larson et al., 2020; Prakash et al., 2021; Angert, 2005; Keim et al., 2004; Koyama et al., 1977), fracture driven by maximum entropy packing statistics may be relevant to organisms other than snowflake yeast.
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies

claim: Noise in developmental geometry may be an inevitable consequence of almost any microscopic mechanism.
source: The broad distributions in cellular volumes we have found in two very different types of organisms, with two very different modes of reproduction and growth, suggest that noise in developmental geometry may be an inevitable consequence of almost any microscopic mechanism.
evidence: Interpretation based on findings from two different organisms

claim: Measurements of the flow fields around Volvox colonies have shown that despite the discreteness of the flagella, the flow is remarkably smooth.
source: Measurements of the flow fields around micropipette-held (Short et al., 2006) and freely-swimming colonies (Drescher et al., 2010a) have shown that despite the discreteness of the flagella, the flow is remarkably smooth, albeit often displaying metachronal waves (Brumley et al., 2015), long-wavelength phase modulations of the beating pattern.
evidence: Supported by citations to Short et al., 2006, Drescher et al., 2010a, and Brumley et al., 2015

claim: Volvox motility is largely unaffected by fluctuations in cell area.
source: Here, we show in fact that Volvox motility is largely unaffected by fluctuations in cell area, indicating that area heterogeneity may not be detrimental to the organism's swimming fitness.
evidence: Conclusion from theoretical analysis

claim: Each of the somatic cells at the surface of a Volvox colony has two flagella that beat at ~30 Hz.
source: Each of the somatic cells at the surface of a Volvox colony has two flagella that beat at ∼30 Hz, in planes that are primarily oriented in the anterior-posterior (AP) direction but with a slight lateral tilt that makes each colony spin around its AP axis.
evidence: Description of Volvox flagellar beating based on established knowledge

claim: Snowflake yeast clusters were grown for approximately 24 hr in YPD liquid medium at 30°C.
source: All experiments were performed on yeast grown for approximately 24 hr in 10 mL of yeast peptone dextrose (YPD, 10 g/L yeast extract, 20 g/L peptone, and 20 g/L dextrose) liquid medium at 30 C, and shaken at 250 rpm in a Symphony Incubating Orbital Shaker model 3,500I.
evidence: Description of experimental growth conditions

claim: 20 snowflake yeast clusters were analyzed using serial block face scanning electron microscopy.
source: This process allowed us to determine the 3D structure of N=20 snowflake yeast clusters and locate cell centers with nanometer precision.
evidence: Description of experimental methods

claim: 9,100 snowflake yeast clusters were simulated, each growing for 7 generations of cell division.
source: To compare exhaustively the distribution of Voronoi volumes between simulations and the k-gamma distribution, we simulated 9,100 clusters. In each simulation, clusters were allowed to grow for 7 generations of cell division, corresponding to an average of 94.2±10.9 cells per cluster.
evidence: Description of simulation methods

claim: 10 Volvox-like groups with N=1000 cells were simulated.
source: We simulated 10 Volvox-like groups with N=1000 cells confined to the surface of a sphere.
evidence: Description of simulation methods

claim: The k-gamma distribution outperformed normal, log-normal, and beta-prime distributions in predicting Voronoi volume distributions.
source: We observed that the k-gamma distribution outperformed the other distributions at every sample size.
evidence: Comparison of different distribution models

claim: The k-gamma distribution estimated the experimentally observed skewness with only a 7% error.
source: We then compared this value to experimentally-measured skewness, finding that the k-gamma distribution estimated the experimentally observed skewness with only a 7% error; the other three distributions estimated the skewness with percent errors of −100%,96%,and174% for the normal, log-normal, and beta-prime distributions, respectively (Figure 2).
evidence: Quantitative comparison shown in Figure 2
